course_name_en: FUNDAMENTALS OF AUTOMATIC CONTROL AND SYSTEMS

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge for modeling mechanical, thermal, and electrical systems for the purpose of control system design.
Knowledge of the main methods for system analysis.
Knowledge of the main methods for designing feedback control systems.
Ability to design control system architectures.
Ability to use software tools for analysis, design, and simulation of dynamic systems.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of linear systems, in the time and frequency domain
Static and dynamic specifications in control systems
Controller design in the frequency domain
Examples of modeling real dynamic systems (mechanical, thermal, and electrical system). Input-output models. Linear, stationary, finite-dimensional models.
Representation and analysis of continuous-time linear systems with Laplace transform. Modes of a continuous-time linear system. Stability.

Analysis of the Step Response of first and second-order systems. Transient response; Steady-state response; Analysis of response to sinusoidal inputs, Harmonic Response, Bode diagrams, Nyquist diagram. Dominant pole models

Open-loop control, feedback control, disturbance compensation, feedforward control. Properties of feedback systems: sensitivity and sensitivity functions to parametric variations, disturbance rejection, improvement of dynamic behavior, effects of process and measurement noise.

Stability of feedback systems and general conditions in the time domain and frequency domain. Routh criterion, Nyquist criterion in continuous-time systems. Stability margins, Conditional stability and under perturbed conditions. Region error and system type.
Root locus for the analysis of continuous-time systems. Root locus plotting rules. Study of the effects of pole and zero movement. Use of the root locus for stabilization and synthesis.

Specifications and fidelity of static and dynamic response. Translation of specifications from the time domain to the frequency domain. General approach to the problem of control system synthesis. Controller design in the frequency domain with graphical methods using Bode diagrams.
Elements of Matlab Programming to understand how to replicate the various simulation examples presented in the course.
teaching_methods: Classroom exercises with MATLAB and Simulink simulation tools
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test, both mandatory. The written test lasts 3 hours and includes 2 exercises and one open question. The exercises verify understanding of analysis and design tools and ability to present results synthetically. The oral test, usually a few days after the written exam, assesses comprehension of topics and ability to present them rigorously and clearly.
bibliography: P. Bolzern, R. Scattolini, N. Schiavoni :Fondamenti di controlli automatici 3/ed Mc Graw-Hill, 2008 (o edizioni successive)
